tagline: Along the big Sabine lake, through the old Neutral Strip.
intro: Toledo Bend Reservoir backs the Sabine River up along the Texas line, 185,000 acres of water, the largest man-made lake in the South. The byway keeps to the Louisiana side for about 78 miles, a rolling road through pine and hardwood forest, with parks, marinas, fishing resorts and lookouts for eagles and blue herons along the way.

After the Louisiana Purchase this was the Neutral Strip, land the United States and Spain agreed to keep free of soldiers while they argued over the line. It went without government or law until the treaty of 1819 set the border at the Sabine.
season: Spring and summer, when the wildflowers and native trees bloom along the road.

moments.title: South Toledo Bend State Park
moments.text: On a few small bluffs above the reservoir, the park is a nesting ground for bald eagles and a favorite of the bass fishermen.

moments.title: Fort Jesup
moments.text: Colonel Zachary Taylor set up the post in 1822 to bring order to the Neutral Strip, and its original field kitchen still stands beside a replica of the officers' quarters.

moments.title: Logansport
moments.text: When the Sabine was the border with the Republic of Texas, surveyors set markers along it, and the one at Logansport is the only known international boundary marker inside the United States.
